title: fastpath: add gating and precision toggle with safe-mode fallback for correctness/perf tradeoffs
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce fast-path gating and precision toggle with safe-mode fallback: allows aggressive FP16/INT8 fast kernels to be opt-in with an automatic correctness-safe fallback. Default behavior unchanged for hosted; opt-in via runtime.flags.fastpath_enable and runtime.flags.safe_mode for Dedicated/Private.
body:
Motivation: We have an existing fast-path kernel set that provides ~15-25% P50 token latency improvements on typical prompt mixes but occasionally produces correctness deltas on edge-case operator patterns (rotary embedding corner cases, mixed attention mask shapes, and certain KV cache invalidation sequences). This PR introduces a small runtime gating layer and an operator-precision toggle that lets us enable the aggressive fast kernels while automatically falling back to the slow, reference implementation for inputs that are outside the safe fast-path subset. This enables teams to opt-in to performance gains without risking silent correctness regressions.

Summary of changes: - runtime/fastpath/gating.rs: new gating logic that inspects the op graph + KV cache hit pattern and decides fast vs slow path per-request. It is lightweight and designed to run in the hot path. - runtime/kernel/precision.rs: adds a precision toggle (fp32|fp16|int8) and a policies table mapping model/operator characteristics to allowed precisions. - runtime/kvcache.rs: KV cache validation hooks so the gating layer can detect stale/invalidated patterns that must go to safe path. - runtime/scheduler.rs: small scheduler changes to ensure fast-path requests are not mixed into request-batch slots that require fallback. Adds a request attribute so batching can keep mixed-mode batches separate when needed. - tests/: new unit and integration tests covering rotary embeddings, attention-mask edge cases, intermittent kv invalidation and per-request fallback metrics. - perf-canary integration: added a canary workload that runs with fastpath enabled and reports correctness/regression metrics. - docs/runtime_flags.md: documents runtime.flags.fastpath_enable, runtime.flags.precision_override, runtime.flags.safe_mode (safe_mode enforces more conservative gating and additional runtime assertions).

Design/Tradeoffs: - Fast-path gating is intentionally conservative: it approves the fast kernel only if the op pattern, attention mask shape, sequence length, kv-cache hit rate, and precision policy all match a known-good profile. This keeps correctness risk low but reduces the raw performance wins on some mixes. The precision toggle allows us to prefer fp16/int8 kernels where they are validated; safe_mode will force fallbacks on ambiguous cases. - There is extra per-request overhead (microseconds) for the gating decision; in our benchmarks this overhead is amortized once the fast kernel executes because the kernel improvement is larger. On very short 1-2 token completions the gating overhead can dominate; safe defaults keep fastpath off for short sequences. - Implementation avoids global state; gating decisions are per-request and cached per-model/sequence-shape for short TTL so subsequent requests benefit.

Behavior and flags: - runtime.flags.fastpath_enable (default: false for hosted, true for dedicated/experimental): global opt-in. - runtime.flags.precision_override (default: "auto"): options: auto|fp32|fp16|int8. auto uses model policy table. - runtime.flags.safe_mode (default: true): when true, gating will err on the side of correctness and run additional validation checks on the slow path before returning. When false, gating is slightly more permissive and permits more fast-paths.

Commits: - 1a3f2d7: add gating infra and tests - 2b9c8f4: precision toggle and model policy table - 7e4d1b2: KV cache validation hooks and scheduler batching separation - 9f0c3a1: docs and perf-canary integration - 5c2e8a0: address reviewer feedback, add regression tests

Files touched (high-level): - runtime/fastpath/gating.rs (new) - runtime/kernel/precision.rs (new) - runtime/kvcache.rs (modified: add validation hooks) - runtime/scheduler.rs (modified: per-request attribute + batching separation) - tests/fastpath/rotary_embedding_edgecase.rs (new) - tests/integration/perf_canary_fastpath.rs (new) - docs/runtime_flags.md (new) - ci/perf-canary.yml (modified) - tools/bench/bench_fastpath.py (new lightweight benchmark harness)

Testing and results: - Unit tests: added new test suite that covers known rotary/attention-mask patterns. All unit tests pass locally and in CI. - Integration/perf-canary: ran the canary against a medium-sized 7B model host; results: P50 token latency improved 18% on the 'typical' prompt mix when fastpath + fp16 are allowed. P95 improved 8%. - Correctness: added differential tests that compare fast vs slow outputs for a curated set of prompts covering embedding rotations and kv invalidation; no diffs observed in safe-mode=on. - CI: initial CI run showed a flaky e2e test (tests/e2e/streaming_timeout.rs) which was unrelated; we re-ran the job and it passed. Final CI status: pass.

Review conversation (highlights): - Miguel Santos: "This looks promising, Aisha. Can you expand on how the gating cache TTL is chosen and what the memory cost is?" -> Author: "Added comment and unit test for TTL behavior. TTL is 30s by default and bounded to 1024 entries per model; memory overhead measured ~40KB/model on typical profiles." - Yuki Nakamura: "Concerned about mixed-batch scheduling. If a fast-path request shares a batch with a fallback request we could violate kernel assumptions." -> Author: "Scheduler now attaches a request.flag.fastpath_mode and batches are formed by compatible modes; fallback: we separated batching slots for mixed traffic. Added integration test to ensure no mixed-mode batch is executed." - Tasha Brown: "We need telemetry to measure how often safe-mode triggers and how often we fall back. Can you add metrics?" -> Author: "Added runtime.metrics.fastpath_attempts, fastpath_successes, fastpath_fallback_reasons and wired them into perf-canary reporting." - Miguel (approve): "LGTM after nits addressed" - Yuki (approve): "Approved; good coverage on rotary cases"

Follow-ups: - ENG-2610: broaden model policy table to cover more model families; planned follow-up PR. - Add a canary dashboard to Redwood Console that surfaces fastpath_fallback_reasons (tracking ticket in Linear).

Migration / Rollout plan: - Merge as feature flagged: fastpath_enable default false for hosted customers. - Roll to Dedicated experimental clusters first with safe_mode=true. - Monitor metrics for 2 weeks; if regression free, consider enabling for additional clusters or flipping precision_override to prefer fp16 for specific model variants.

Notes about correctness: This PR intentionally does not change any default behavior for hosted customers. The safe-mode and gating logic are conservative and instrumented. We included multiple regression tests to reduce risk of silent correctness drift.

Merge: Squash-and-merge after approvals and CI green.

If you'd like I can split the gating infra and precision policy table into two smaller PRs, but keeping them together made it easier to add end-to-end tests and perf-canary measurements.
